doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Chicago and New York with Dizzy Gillespie
title: Destitute in Chicago and Foster Johnson's studio
summary: After leaving the hospital he slept in the streets until a dancer, Foster Johnson, gave him studio space.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So that was the six months. I left. I went to Chicago. Slept in the streets a little bit. I finally ran into a very sweet guy, Foster, a dancer, Foster – it’ll come to me. Anyway, this guy had a studio, because he went with – Foster Johnson – he went with a woman who – what do you call a head of a . . .?
Yeah, brothel is more like it. What?
Madame. She was the madame in Chicago.
